narrative:
The 2017 New York Yankees arrived at spring training with modest expectations, a roster in transition between dynasty and rebuild, and a front office quietly excited about a wave of young talent. What followed was one of the most entertaining and emotionally turbulent seasons in recent Yankee memory. April set the tone immediately, with clutch home runs from Aaron Hicks and Starlin Castro and a walk-off single by Didi Gregorius signaling that this team had a flair for the dramatic. A 15-8 start was the best medicine for any lingering doubts about the direction of the franchise.

May and June told a more complicated story. Brett Gardner delivered one of the season's most electrifying swings with a three-run bomb on May 5th, but the bullpen — usually a strength — began to leak. Aroldis Chapman hit batters, Dellin Betances surrendered crushing singles, and a disastrous mid-June stretch saw the Yankees stumble through Oakland and lose three winnable games in ways that felt almost scripted for maximum pain. June finished 13-15, the only losing month of the season, and the club looked vulnerable at exactly the wrong time.

July and August proved the Yankees were made of sterner stuff. The trade deadline brought reinforcements, and the lineup — anchored by Aaron Judge's historic rookie season and punctuated by Brett Gardner's relentless clutch hitting — ground out enough wins to keep pace in the Wild Card race. Even when Chapman or the bullpen stumbled in August, the offense answered. A blazing 20-8 September erased any doubt about the playoffs, as the Baby Bombers announced themselves to the baseball world with authority.

The postseason was a showcase and a heartbreak in equal measure. The Yankees dispatched Cleveland in the Division Series in thrilling fashion, with Aaron Hicks homering and the young roster rising to the moment. But the ALCS brought the Houston Astros — the best team in baseball — and with them came Carlos Correa, Jose Altuve, and a relentless offense that exposed the Yankees' bullpen vulnerabilities one final time. Chapman was touched again, Robertson couldn't hold leads, and the Astros closed out New York in seven games. It stung, but the 2017 Yankees had given their fans something rare: a season full of genuine joy, legitimate contention, and a glimpse of a dynasty being born.

chapters.title: Fast Out of the Gate
chapters.description: A 15-8 April fueled by clutch home runs and late-game heroics announced the Yankees as legitimate contenders from the very first weeks.

chapters.title: Bulletin Board Material
chapters.description: May brought Gardner's big blast but also the first signs of bullpen fragility, as Chapman and the relievers began giving back hard-earned leads.

chapters.title: The Roughest Month
chapters.description: A 13-15 June exposed real cracks in the roster, with a string of brutal bullpen meltdowns turning winnable games into demoralizing losses.

chapters.title: Grinding Through Summer
chapters.description: July and August were uneven but productive, with Gardner, Sánchez, and the offense repeatedly bailing out a bullpen that remained maddeningly inconsistent.

chapters.title: September Surge
chapters.description: A scorching 20-8 September erased all doubt, as the Baby Bombers locked up a playoff spot with the kind of sustained excellence that hinted at something special.

chapters.title: October Dreams, Astros Reality
chapters.description: The Yankees thrilled in the Division Series before running into the buzzsaw Houston Astros in the ALCS, where familiar bullpen demons ended a magical season one round short of the World Series.
